newsitem.title: UK: Britain's "top people" back Charles marrying - poll.
newsitem.headline: Britain's "top people" back Charles marrying - poll.

text.p: The vast majority of Britain's "top people" believe Prince Charles should be able to marry whoever he likes, according to an opinion poll published on Wednesday.
The Times poll, a major boost to Charles' increasingly open affair with Camilla Parker Bowles, was conducted among cabinet ministers, leading businessmen, academics and newspaper editors.
Eighty-two percent said he should not give up his right to the throne if he were to remarry and 83 percent said he should remarry whoever he likes.
This contrasts sharply with the view of The Archbishop of Canterbury who said on Tuesday that the Church of England would be thrown into crisis if the divorced heir-to-the-throne remarried.
George Carey, on a visit to Australia, said the fact that Charles had divorced Princess Diana posed no obstacle to the throne. But the issue of remarriage was very different.
As king, Charles would become the head of the Church of England which disapproves of remarriage after a monarch's divorce. Carey is the church's spiritual leader.
